experiment_data.hypothesis: Pooling samples from two different fine-tuned models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-8B) for entity construction significantly outperforms single-model construction because cross-model diversity breaks model-specific mode collapse, reducing degeneracy and providing complementary error patterns that improve consensus quality.
experiment_data.notes: B5 cross-model consistency on SciERC NER. Mixed pool (4 Qwen + 4 LLaMA) significantly outperforms pure LLaMA construction (+0.42pp uniform, p=0.000, CI [0.27,0.58]). Cross-model diversity reduces degeneracy (11.6% vs LLaMA 23.4%). Most of the +4.37pp ΔF1 vs Qwen greedy comes from LLaMA being stronger (greedy 0.784 vs 0.748), but the +0.42pp vs pure LLaMA is genuine cross-model diversity gain. Supports diversity hypothesis: different models make complementary errors → better consensus.
